method: A Linux device number is a 12-bit major and a 20-bit minor, so the page refuses a major above 4095 or a minor above 1048575 instead of silently truncating it. The input is auto-detected: a pair with one colon (the /proc/partitions and lsblk form), a pair with one comma (the ls -l device column), a run of digits (a decimal dev_t), or a 0x-prefixed value (a hex dev_t); anything else is refused with the accepted forms in the message. Userspace packs the pair with glibc makedev, which keeps the major in bits 8 to 19, the low minor byte in bits 0 to 7 and minor bits 8 to 19 in bits 20 to 31; the page also reports the kernel MKDEV value, major times 1048576 plus minor, because the two layouts differ and only the first is what stat, ls and mknod use. Device numbers whose minor needs the high field (above 255) exercise the split directly, for example 8:300 becoming 0x10082c. The major table follows the kernel devices.txt registry: memory devices, TTY and alternate TTY devices, misc devices, input core, Unix98 PTY masters and slaves, USB devices and USB serial, DRI, RAM disks, loop devices, SCSI disks, metadisks, SCSI CD-ROM and MMC, plus the dynamic and local ranges 234-254 and 240-254. Node names are derived only where the registry documents the mapping: sd letters use 16 minors per disk (8:17 is sdb1), MMC cards use the default 8-minor stride, UART ports start 64 minors after the virtual consoles, and the input core splits joystick, mouse and event minors on 32-minor boundaries. Majors that appear in both tables, such as 1, are reported as ambiguous rather than given one node, and an unregistered major says so instead of guessing a driver. Everything is computed locally with integer arithmetic: no network access, uploads or storage.

sources.title: Linux kernel Documentation/admin-guide/devices.txt: the registry of major numbers, the names and node numbers used by the table, and the note that 259 block is a dynamic extended major.
makedev(3) from the Linux man-pages: makedev combines a major and minor into a dev_t, and major() and minor() split the st_rdev or st_dev value returned by stat(2).
glibc misc/sys/sysmacros.h: the exact gnu_dev_makedev and gnu_dev_major bit layout reproduced on this page, with the major in bits 8 to 19 and the minor split across bits 0 to 7 and 20 to 31.
Linux kernel include/linux/kdev_t.h: MINORBITS is 20, so MKDEV packs the major above the minor and the two encodings differ for the same pair.
